idiom_name: Leaf (Vapor) templates with # tags over an Encodable context struct
implementation_notes: Swift has no template syntax in the language, so server-side rendering goes through an engine such as Leaf (Vapor's default) or Stencil. Leaf templates use #tags - #(variable), #for, #if, #extend/#export/#import - over a context that must be an Encodable value, so the model reaches the view as typed, already-fetched data and the idiomatic flow keeps the fetching half of the pattern out of the template; #unsafeHTML is the explicit raw-output switch. The script-in-the-view form remains justified for small HTML and email fragments where the data is in hand, while a context struct prepared by the route handler is the maintainable shape.
pitfalls: The context must be Encodable and heterogeneous dictionaries are not supported, so wrapping values in a struct is mandatory; passing the wrong shape fails at render time.
#unsafeHTML inserts markup verbatim - every user-controlled value must go through #(...) instead, and the difference is one tag name.
Templates are resolved by name from the configured views directory, so a missing or misspelled template is a request-time failure unless the app pre-validates templates at boot.
Rendering on a blocking thread stalls the event loop; Vapor expects rendering inside the request's async context, and doing synchronous file work per render wastes the template cache.
